workEn: Popol Vuh (The Council Book of the K'iche' Maya)
title: Ta xqui nohih chic vchicopil huyub
titleEn: Popol Vuh — The animals, and the people of mud
part: The animals, and the people of mud
source: Popol Vuh, “The animals, and the people of mud”, from the only surviving copy: the K'iche' text in the hand of Fray Francisco Ximénez, written at Chichicastenango c. 1701–1703 (Newberry Library, Chicago, Ayer MS 1515, fols. 2v–4r, left-hand column), read from the Library of Congress / World Digital Library images; public domain. The text is the manuscript's own spelling, including the colonial letters ꜩ (tz), ꜯ (tz'), ꜭ (k'), ꜭh (ch') and ꜫ (q'), v for u and w, z for s, h for j, and c/qu for both k and q. Where Ximénez's cursive makes these letters hard to tell apart, the reading of Brasseur de Bourbourg's edition (Paris, 1861), made from the same manuscript, was used as a check. Word division, punctuation, capitals and quotation marks are editorial. The ꜩ→tz button shows every word in the modern K'iche' alphabet; there an ejective or glottal stop the scribe left unmarked is supplied where the word is certain, and a word whose modern form is uncertain is simply respelled. Pronunciation: modern K'iche' values for the modern spelling, an admitted convention. No prepared audio yet. All translations were made fresh from the K'iche' for Lectorium.

sentences.t: Ta xqui nohih chic vchicopil huyub, chahal re quichelah ronohel; vvinaquil huyub ri: quieh, ꜯiquin, ꜭoh, balam, cumaꜩ, zochoh, canti, chahal caam.
sentences.l: Then they conceived now its-animals of-mountain, guardians of forest all; its-people of-mountain these: deer, bird, puma, jaguar, snake, rattlesnake, canti, guardian of-vines.
sentences.i: Then they conceived the animals of the mountains, the guardians of all the forests, the people of the mountains: the deer and the birds, the puma and the jaguar, the snake, the rattlesnake and the canti, the guardian of the vines.
sentences.n: The second episode: the animals. vchicopil huyub 'the animals of the mountain': chicop 'animal' with v- 'its' and -il, which makes the animals belong to the mountain; vvinaquil huyub, built the same way on vinac 'person', calls them the mountain's people. chahal 'guardian, keeper' (from chah 'guard'). queh (here quieh) is the deer, balam the jaguar, cumaꜩ the snake (the second half of Ꜫucumaꜩ), zochoh the rattlesnake. ꜭoh is taken as the puma (Brasseur 'lion'); Ximénez's letter looks like the cuatrillo, but the word is koj in modern dictionaries, with plain k, and the toggle shows koj. canti is a venomous snake (Brasseur: beautiful and very dangerous); Ximénez writes plain c where Brasseur has q (= ꜭ), and the toggle respells the letters as written. quichelah 'forest' is spelled as in the first part, though Brasseur reads a g (= ꜫ) in it here. chahal caam 'guardian of the vines' may be one more creature or a title closing the list; uncertain.

sentences.t: Cacha ri Alom, Ꜭaholom: “Xa pa chi lolinic, ma xa on chi ꜯininic vxe che, caam? Cate vꜩ chi ꜭohe chahal re,” xeꜭha cut, ta xqui nohih, xqui ꜩihoh puch.
sentences.l: Says the Child-Bearer, Son-Begetter: “Only (is-it) to be-calm, or only perhaps to be-silent the-foot of-tree, vine? Then good that there-be guardians of-it,” they-said then, as they conceived-it, they told-it also.
sentences.i: Then the Mother of children and the Father of sons says: “Is the foot of the trees and vines to be only calm, only silent? It is good, then, that there should be guardians for them,” they said, as they conceived it and spoke of it.
sentences.n: cacha 'says' is ca-, the marker of an ongoing action, + cha 'say': the story slips into the present. The question is built from xa 'only', ma 'or, is it?' and on 'perhaps'; pa here is not 'in' but seems to carry the question, and the exact sense of xa pa ... ma xa on is inferred. lolinic and ꜯininic 'calm, silent' are two of the words of stillness from the first part, now said of the forest without creatures. vxe che, caam 'the foot of the trees and vines' (vxe 'its root, its base'). cate 'then, only then' (Brasseur qate). chi ꜭohe 'that there be' has chi of wishing. The same speech is brought in with a singular verb (cacha) and closed with a plural one (xeꜭha 'they said'): the creator pair is one and two at once.

sentences.t: Huzu cu xvinaquir queh, ꜯiquin.
sentences.l: Suddenly then came-into-being deer, bird.
sentences.i: And at once the deer and the birds came into being.
sentences.n: Ximénez writes huzucu with one c serving both words: the reading is huzuc cu 'at once, then' (Brasseur divides huzu cu). We print the letters as written, and the toggle shows the full word jusuk. huzuc 'at once' is the word used when the mountains rose in the first part. queh, ꜯiquin 'deer, bird' is a pair that stands for all animals, four-footed and winged.

sentences.t: Ta xqui zipah cut rochoch queh, ꜯiquin: “At, queh, pa be yaa, pa ziuan cat var vi; varal cat ꜭohe vi pa quim, pa zacal, pa quechelah; qui poco vi ivib, cahcah ibinibal, ychacabal.” Chuxic, xe vchaxic.
sentences.l: Then they gave then its-home deer, bird: “You, deer, on road of-water(?), in canyon you-will-sleep there; here you-will-be there in grass, in brush(?), in forest; you-will-multiply there yourselves, four-four your-walking, your-standing(?).” It-shall-be, they-were-told.
sentences.i: Then they gave the deer and the birds their homes: “You, deer, by the paths of the streams, in the canyons you shall sleep; here you shall live, in the grass, in the brush, in the forest; there you shall multiply, on four feet you shall walk, on four feet you shall stand.” So it shall be, they were told.
sentences.n: zipah 'give, present'. rochoch: r- 'its' (before a vowel) + ochoch 'home'. at 'you (one)'; cat is c- (shall) + at, the singular of quix 'you all (shall)'. var 'sleep'. The deer is spoken to as one and then, in ivib 'yourselves' and ibinibal 'your walking', as many: i- is 'your (pl.)'. qui poco vi ivib 'you shall multiply yourselves' is not qui 'their': it is c- (shall) + i- 'you (all)', run together as in quiꜭhava below. yaa is taken as 'water, stream' (Brasseur 'streams'). zacal is unclear: Brasseur reads zacul and gives 'fodder'; 'brush' is a guess. cahcah 'four and four': on all fours. ibinibal 'means of walking' (bin 'walk' + -ibal, like vxenabal in the first part); ychacabal is taken as its pair, 'means of standing', which is inferred (Ximénez writes plain c where Brasseur has k, that is q). chuxic 'it shall be' (ch- + ux 'become'; compare chuxoc 'let it be') and xe vchaxic 'they were told' follow the speech. quechelah 'forest' is a second spelling of quichelah.

sentences.t: Ta xqui chi cut cochoch chuti ꜯiquin, nima ꜯiquin: “Ix, ix ꜯiquin, chuvi che, chuvi caam quix ochochin vi, quix hain vi; chiri quix poc vi, quix quiritah vi chuꜫab che, chuꜫab caam,” xe vꜭhaxic quieh, ꜯiquin.
sentences.l: Then they [gave] again then their-homes small bird, great bird: “You, you birds, on-top-of tree, on-top-of vine you-will-make-home there, you-will-make-house there; there you-will-multiply, you-will-spread-out(?) there on-the-arm of-tree, on-the-arm of-vine,” they-were-told deer, bird.
sentences.i: Then they gave the birds their homes as well, the small birds and the great: “You birds, in the tops of the trees, in the tops of the vines you shall make your homes, you shall make your houses; there you shall multiply, there you shall spread out, on the branches of the trees, on the branches of the vines,” the deer and the birds were told.
sentences.n: Shared letters again: Ximénez writes xquichicut, and the likely reading is xqui chic cut 'they (did) again, then', with one c for two words (Brasseur divides x-quichic cut); we print xqui chi cut. No verb root follows xqui, so zipah 'give' seems to be understood from the sentence before; Brasseur supplies it too. cochoch 'their homes': qui- 'their' becomes c- before a vowel. chuvi 'on top of' (chi + v- 'its' + vi 'head, top') and chuꜫab 'on the arm of' (ꜫab 'hand, arm'), that is, the branches: relational nouns made from parts of the body. ochochin and hain both mean 'make one's home' (ochoch and ha 'house'), a couplet; quiritah 'spread out' is inferred. xe vꜭhaxic 'they were told': ꜭha 'say' + -x passive, with ꜭh for ch' (vchaxic above has plain ch).

sentences.t: Ta xqui bano qui banoh; ronohel xu camo vvarabal, vyacalibal.
sentences.l: Then they did their doing; all it-took its-sleeping-place, its-standing-place.
sentences.i: Then they did what was theirs to do, and each one took its place to sleep, its place to rest.
sentences.n: xqui bano qui banoh 'they did their doing': a verb with its own noun, meaning they did what they were made for. xu camo 'it took': xu- is x- + v- 'it' as subject of a verb with an object, the singular of xqui; ronohel 'all' is treated as one. The c of camo has a small hook and might be ꜫ; the word is cam 'take', as in xchicacam in the first part (modern k'am). vvarabal 'place of sleeping' (var 'sleep' + -abal) and vyacalibal 'place of standing, of resting' (the root of yacalic in the first part) are a couplet for a lair.

sentences.t: Quehe cut cochoch vi chicop ri vleu xu yao Alom, Ꜭaholom. Xuꜩininaca chic ronohel ri queh, ꜯiquin.
sentences.l: Thus then their-homes the animals of-the earth it-gave Child-Bearer, Son-Begetter. Had-been-completed now all the deer, bird.
sentences.i: So it was that the Mother of children and the Father of sons gave the animals of the earth their homes. Now the deer and the birds were all complete.
sentences.n: xu yao 'gave (it)': ya 'give' with the singular xu-, though Alom, Ꜭaholom are two titles; the creator pair is often treated as one being. Xuꜩininaca 'they had been completed' is built on utzin 'complete, make good' (from vꜩ 'good'), as in xchuꜩinic in the first part, with the perfect ending -inac (compare petenac 'having come'); the exact form is uncertain.

sentences.t: Ta xe vꜭhax chi cut ry queh, ꜯiquin rumal Ꜯacol, Bitol, Alom, Ꜭaholom: “Quix ꜭhauoc, quix ziquinoc; mix yonoloquinic, mix ziquinic; quix ꜭhavahe tah chi huhunal, chu hutac chobil, chi hutac molahil,” xe vꜭhaxic ri queh, ꜯiquin, ꜭoh, balam, cumaꜩ.
sentences.l: Then they-were-told again then the deer, bird by Builder, Shaper, Child-Bearer, Son-Begetter: “You-shall-speak, you-shall-call; just-now cry(?), just-now call; you-speak let each-one, according-to each division, by each gathering,” they-were-told the deer, bird, puma, jaguar, snake.
sentences.i: Then the deer and the birds were spoken to again by the Builder and the Shaper, the Mother of children and the Father of sons: “Speak, call out! Now that you can cry, now that you can call, speak each one of you, each after its kind, each after its flock,” so they told the deer, the birds, the puma, the jaguar, the snake.
sentences.n: Ximénez writes chicut again, one c for chic cut 'again, then'. quix ꜭhauoc, quix ziquinoc 'speak, call out': quix 'you all (shall)' with -oc, the ending of what is wished and not yet real (as in chuxoc 'let it be'). ꜭhau 'speak' is the verb of xꜭhau in the first part; ziquin 'call, call upon' is what the creators want: to be called on by name. mix yonoloquinic is doubtful: an ink blot sits between yonolo and quinic, with a stroke above like an i-dot (Brasseur yonoliquinic); the word is unknown, and 'cry' is a guess from its pair ziquinic. mix is taken as mi- 'just now' + x-, as in mixatulic in the first part. chi huhunal 'each one', hun 'one' doubled: Ximénez wrote the second hu above the line, and it is printed in place. hutac 'each'; chobil 'division' (chob 'divide') and molahil 'gathering' (mol 'gather'): 'each by its kind'.

sentences.t: “Chi byih na cut ri cabi, coh icaharizah, oh ichuch, oh icahau.
sentences.l: “Let-(you)-say now then the our-name, us you-shall-praise(?), we your-mother, we your-father.
sentences.i: “Say our name, then, praise us, we who are your mother, we who are your father.
sentences.n: A verb with two persons: coh icaharizah is c- (shall) + oh 'us' + i- 'you (all)' + caharizah, 'you shall praise(?) us'. The one acted on comes first, then the doer. caharizah is not otherwise known (Ximénez writes plain c where Brasseur reads g, that is ꜫ); 'praise, honour' is inferred from the context and Brasseur's French. oh 'we'; ichuch, icahau 'your mother, your father': the creators are mother and father at once, as in the preamble. byih is a doubtful reading: the letters look like byyh, and Brasseur prints biyh here and byih later; we print byih both times. It is bih 'say' (modern b'ij, as in vbixic 'its being said'); the toggle respells the letters as written.

sentences.t: Quiꜭhava na cut Huracan, Chipi Caculha, Raxa Caculha, Vꜭux Cah, Vꜭux Vleuh, Ꜯacol, Bitol, Alom, Ꜭaholom; quix ꜭhaoc, coh iziquih, coh iꜫihila,” xe vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: Call-upon now then Huracan, Youngest Thunderbolt, Green Thunderbolt, Heart of-Sky, Heart of-Earth, Builder, Shaper, Child-Bearer, Son-Begetter; you-shall-speak, us you-call, us you-honour,” they-were-told.
sentences.i: Call upon Huracan, Youngest Thunderbolt, Green Thunderbolt, Heart of Sky, Heart of Earth, the Builder and the Shaper, the Mother of children and the Father of sons; speak, call on us, honour us,” they were told.
sentences.n: The roll of names the animals were meant to recite: Huracan and the two Thunderbolts, who together are the Heart of Sky, then Heart of Earth and the two pairs of titles. quiꜭhava 'call upon (them)': ꜭhava 'speak to' with c- and i- 'you (all)'. ꜭhaoc is ꜭhauoc 'speak' without its u. iꜫihila 'you honour (us)' is the verb behind vꜫihilabal 'its glory' in the first part, from ꜫih 'day, sun': to honour someone is to keep his day. Ximénez's q-shaped letter is read ꜫ, as Brasseur's g. ziquih and ꜫihila, calling and honouring, are what the creators ask for throughout this part.

sentences.t: Ma cu xuꜩinic xeꜭhauic quehe ta ri vinac; xa que vachelahic, xa que caralahic, xa que vohonic; mavi xvachinic vvach qui ꜭhabal; halahoh xcoꜫibeh chi qui huhunal.
sentences.l: Not then it-succeeded they-spoke like the person; only they-kept screeching(?), only they-kept chattering(?), only they-kept howling(?); not it-bore-fruit its-face their-speech; differently they-cried(?) each one-of-them.
sentences.i: But they could not speak as people do; they could only screech, only chatter, only howl; their speech never took shape, and each one cried out in its own way.
sentences.n: ma cu ... xuꜩinic 'but it did not come right' (the manuscript has xuꜩinic; Brasseur prints x-utzitic): utzin 'succeed, complete', from vꜩ 'good'. que here is c- (ongoing) + e 'they', not que 'thus': 'they kept on ...'. vachelahic, caralahic and vohonic are animal noises; which noise each one names is a guess. mavi xvachinic vvach 'its face did not appear': vachin 'bear fruit, show itself' is built on vach 'face, fruit', so their speech never took form. halahoh 'different, of many kinds'; xcoꜫibeh 'cried out' is inferred (Brasseur 'murmuring'). chi qui huhunal 'each one of them'.

sentences.t: Ta xqui ta ri Ꜯacol, Bitol mavi mixuꜩinic, mixeꜭhauic; xeꜭha chic chi quibil quib: “Mavi mixuꜩin vbixic cabi rumal, oh cahꜯac, oh pu cahbit. Mavi vꜩ,” xꜭha chic chi quibil quib ri Alom, Ꜭaholom.
sentences.l: Then they heard the Builder, Shaper not it-had-succeeded, they-had-spoken; they-said again to themselves among-themselves: “Not it-has-succeeded its-saying our-name by-it, we their-builders, we also their-shapers. Not good,” said again to themselves among-themselves the Child-Bearer, Son-Begetter.
sentences.i: When the Builder and the Shaper heard that it had not come right, that they had not spoken, they said to one another: “They have not been able to say our name, though we are their builders and their shapers. This is not good,” said the Mother of children and the Father of sons to one another.
sentences.n: xqui ta 'they heard': here ta is the verb 'hear', not the particle. mi- before x- marks what has just happened: mixuꜩinic 'it has (just) come right', mixeꜭhauic 'they have (just) spoken'. chi quibil quib 'among themselves, to one another'. vbixic 'its being said', a passive noun from bi 'say'; rumal 'by it' is singular, the animals taken together. cahꜯac, cahbit 'their builders, their shapers': c- is qui- 'their' before a vowel (as cochoch 'their homes') + ahꜯac, ahbit, with ah- 'one who'; the creators take these titles later in this part.

sentences.t: Xe vꜭhax cut: “Xa quix halatahic, rumal mavi mixuꜩinic, mavi mixix ꜭhauic.
sentences.l: They-were-told then: “Only you-shall-be-changed, because not it-has-succeeded, not you-have-spoken.
sentences.i: And they were told: “You shall be changed, because it has not come right, because you have not spoken.
sentences.n: halatahic 'be changed': hal 'change' + -atah, the same passive ending as in xbanatah 'it was done'. mixix ꜭhauic shows the person marker in full: mi- + x- + ix 'you (all)' + ꜭhau 'speak'.

sentences.t: Mi cu xca hal caꜩih: ivecha, icuxun, ivarabal, iyacalibal xivech vi; mixe vuxic ziuan, quechelah, rumal mavi xuꜩin caꜫihiloxic; mavi ix ziquiy.
sentences.l: Now then we-have-changed our-word: your-food, your-fodder(?), your-sleeping-place, your-standing-place became-yours there; have-become canyon, forest, because not it-succeeded our-being-honoured; not you callers.
sentences.i: We have changed our word now: your food and your fodder, your places to sleep and your places to rest, are yours there; they have become the canyons and the forests, because you could not honour us; you do not call on us.
sentences.n: xca hal 'we have changed': ca- 'we' as subject of the verb, the same prefix that means 'our' in caꜩih 'our word'. ivecha 'your food' and icuxun (sense guessed: 'fodder, pasture'; Brasseur 'nourishment') pair with ivarabal, iyacalibal, the lairs given earlier. xivech 'became yours' (ech 'possession' with iv- 'your'). mixe vuxic 'they have become' (ux 'become', as in xuxic): the animals' places are now the wild. caꜫihiloxic 'our being honoured', a passive noun from ꜫihila; ziquiy 'caller', an agent noun from ziquih 'call'.

sentences.t: Que ca ꜭo, co vi lo ꜫihilonel, nimanel; chi ca ban chic.
sentences.l: They yet-are(?), there-are there perhaps honourers, obeyers; let we make now.
sentences.i: There will yet be others, there must be some who will honour us and obey us; let us make them now.
sentences.n: co vi lo is ꜭo vi 'there is' with -lo 'perhaps', as in naquilalo; Ximénez writes plain c where Brasseur has q (= ꜭ). ꜫihilonel 'one who honours' and nimanel 'one who obeys' (from nim 'great': nima 'obey, hold great') are agent nouns in -nel: the beings the creators want. chi ca ban 'let us make': chi of wishing + ca- 'we'. The opening que ca ꜭo is unclear; it is taken as 'there will yet be'.

sentences.t: Xa chi cam ipatan; xa itiohil chi cachic; ta chuxoc.
sentences.l: Only let-(you)-take your-service; only your-flesh let-it-be-chewed(?); so let-it-be.
sentences.i: Take up your service, and only that: your flesh shall be eaten. So be it.
sentences.n: patan 'service, duty, tribute': what a subject owes his lord. tiohil 'flesh, meat'; Ximénez's ꜩ-like ligature stands here for ti, as Brasseur reads it. chi cachic 'let it be chewed' is inferred from Brasseur's French ('crushed under the tooth'); the root is not otherwise known. This is the animals' fate: since they cannot give the creators words, they give their flesh.

sentences.t: Are cut chi patanih,” xe vꜭhaxic, ta xe pixabaxic chuti chicop, nima chicop ꜭo chuvach vleu.
sentences.l: This then let-it-serve,” they-were-told, then they-were-charged small animal, great animal there-is on-the-face-of earth.
sentences.i: “This shall be your service,” they were told, and so the small animals and the great, all that are on the face of the earth, were given their charge.
sentences.n: chi patanih 'let it serve': patan 'service' made into a verb with -ih. xe pixabaxic 'they were charged': pixab 'counsel, command', the formal charge an elder gives the young, + passive -ax. chuvach 'on the face of' = chi + v- 'its' + vach 'face', another relational noun.

sentences.t: Ta xrah cu qui tih chic qui ꜫih; xrah qui tihtobeh chic; xrah pu qui nuc chic ꜫihilabal.
sentences.l: Then it-wanted then their trying again their day; it-wanted their testing again; it-wanted also their arranging again honouring.
sentences.i: Then a new trial of their day was wanted: that they should make another attempt, that they should set in order a new way of honouring.
sentences.n: xrah 'wanted' is x- + r- 'he, it' (the ergative prefix before a vowel) + ah 'want': the verb is singular, and the wanted action follows as a noun with qui- 'their': qui tih 'their trying'. Who wanted is not said. It may be the creators, often spoken of as one (as with xu yao above), wanting the animals to try again, or it may be impersonal, 'it was wished'; Brasseur makes the animals the subject ('they wanted'), which the singular verb does not show. tih and tihtobeh 'try, test' (the ligature read ti, as Brasseur). qui ꜫih 'their day': ꜫih is 'day, sun', and here seems to mean their lot or fortune (Brasseur 'fortune'); the sense is inferred. nuc 'arrange, put in order' (Brasseur nuq, that is ꜭ; Ximénez writes plain c). Three lines with one meaning: a triplet built like the couplets.

sentences.t: Xma xqui ta vi qui ꜭhabal chi quibil quib; xma xnauachir vi cut, xma xbanatah vi puch.
sentences.l: Not they-heard there their speech among themselves; not it-took-shape there then, not it-was-done there also.
sentences.i: But they could not understand one another's speech; nothing took shape, nothing was done.
sentences.n: xqui ta 'they heard', here 'understood'. xnauachir 'it took shape, it came to light' is built on vach 'face' with -ir 'become' (as vinaquir from vinac); the sense is inferred. xma 'there was not' with a completive verb: 'it never'.

sentences.t: Quehe cut xe chacatah vi qui tiohil; xqui patanih; xe tiyic, xe camizaxic ri chicop ꜭo varal chuvach vleuh.
sentences.l: Thus then they were-overcome(?) there their flesh; they served-it; they were-eaten(?), they were-killed the animals there-are here on-the-face-of earth.
sentences.i: And so their flesh was brought low: they served, they were eaten, they were killed, the animals that are here on the face of the earth.
sentences.n: camizaxic 'being killed': cam 'die' + -iza 'make' + -x passive, 'be made to die'. xe tiyic is a doubtful reading: the manuscript has the ti-ligature followed by yc or iyc, and Brasseur's OCR is lost at this point; his French ('reduced to being eaten') gives the sense, and tiyic 'were eaten' is a guess from it. chacatah 'was overcome, brought low' is inferred. The sentence explains why animals are hunted: their flesh is the service they could not give in words.

sentences.t: Quehe cut vtihtobexic chic vinac ꜯac, vinac bit cumal Ꜯacol, Bitol, Alom, Ꜭaholom: “Xa cu tiha chic!
sentences.l: Thus then its-being-tried again person built, person shaped by Builder, Shaper, Child-Bearer, Son-Begetter: “Only then try again!
sentences.i: So there came another attempt at a person built, a person shaped, by the Builder and the Shaper, the Mother of children and the Father of sons: “Try once more!
sentences.n: vtihtobexic 'its being tried': tihtob 'try' with the passive noun ending -exic. vinac ꜯac, vinac bit 'person built, person shaped' is the couplet of the creators' wish at the end of the first part. tiha 'try!', with -a, the ending of a command, and no person prefix: the creators urge each other on (compare ca tiha 'let us try' below). The ꜩ-like ligature is read ti in all these words, following Brasseur.

sentences.t: Mix yopih ravaxic, vzaquiric; ca bana ꜩucul que, cool que.
sentences.l: Has-just arrived its-sowing, its-dawning; let-us make provider for-us(?), sustainer for-us(?).
sentences.i: Now the sowing has come, the dawning has come; let us make one who will provide for us, one who will sustain us.
sentences.n: mix yopih 'it has just arrived'. ravaxic 'its sowing' (r- 'its' before a vowel + avax 'sow') and vzaquiric 'its dawning' are the pair of the first part (chauaxoc, zaquiroc): the creators reckon time as farmers do. ca bana 'let us make': ca- 'we' + ban + -a of command. ꜩucul, cool 'provider, sustainer' again; que 'for us' is uncertain.

sentences.t: Hupacha ta coh ziquixoc, ta coh nabax puch chuvach vleuh?
sentences.l: How then we be-called-upon, then we be-remembered(?) also on-the-face-of earth?
sentences.i: How shall we be called upon, how shall we be remembered on the face of the earth?
sentences.n: coh ziquixoc 'we shall be called upon': coh (c- + oh 'we') + ziquih 'call' with the passive -ix and -oc. nabax is its pair; 'be remembered' is inferred (Brasseur 'commemorated').

sentences.t: Mix ca tiho chirech ri nabe caꜯac, cabit; mavi mixuꜩinic caꜫihiloxic, cacalaixic puch cumal.
sentences.l: We-have-just tried-it with-it the first our-built, our-shaped; not it-has-succeeded our-being-honoured, our-being-glorified also by-them.
sentences.i: We have already tried with our first work, what we built and shaped; it did not come right: we were not honoured, we were not glorified by them.
sentences.n: mix ca tiho 'we have tried it': ca- 'we' again as subject. chirech 'with it, about it'. caꜯac, cabit 'our built, our shaped': the pair from the first part, here the animals. cacalaixic 'our being glorified' shares its root with vcalaibal 'its honour' in the first part.

sentences.t: Quehe cut ca tiha vi vbanic ahnim, ahxob, ꜩucul, cool,” xeꜭha.
sentences.l: Thus then let-us-try there its-making obeyer, reverer, provider, sustainer,” they-said.
sentences.i: So let us try to make one who obeys and one who reveres, one who provides and one who sustains,” they said.
sentences.n: ahnim 'one who obeys' (nim, as in nimanel) and ahxob 'one who fears, reveres' (xob 'fear'): agent nouns with ah-. The four words say what a person is for in this book: to obey, to revere, and to provide for and sustain the gods.

sentences.t: Ta vꜯaquic cut, vbanic puch: vleu, xocol vtiohil xqui bano.
sentences.l: Then its-building then, its-making also: earth, mud its-flesh they made.
sentences.i: Then came the building and the making: of earth, of mud they made its flesh.
sentences.n: vꜯaquic, vbanic 'its building, its making': ꜯac is the root of Ꜯacol. vleu, xocol 'earth, mud': the first person is made of wet earth. vtiohil 'its flesh' is the word just used of the animals. A blot before vbanic is a correction by Ximénez; nothing can be read under it.

sentences.t: Ma cu vꜩ xqui lo: xa chi yohomanic, xa ꜩubulic, xa nebelic, xa lubanic, xa vvlanic, xa pu chiumaric; mavi chi colol vholom; xa hum benac vi vvach; xa culuvach, mavi chi mucun chirih.
sentences.l: Not then good they-saw(?)-it: only it-came-undone, only sagged(?), only went-limp(?), only slumped(?), only fell-apart(?), only also grew-sodden; not it-turned(?) its-head; only one-way gone its-face; only veiled(?)-face, not it-looked behind-it.
sentences.i: But they saw that it was not good: it only came undone, only sagged, only went limp, only slumped, only fell apart, only grew sodden; it could not turn its head; its face looked one way only; its sight was veiled, it could not look behind it.
sentences.n: Ma cu vꜩ: the manuscript has macu here (Brasseur prints mavi). xqui lo 'they saw it' follows Brasseur's French ('they saw'); lo is not otherwise known as a verb of seeing, and the sense is inferred. Six verbs with xa 'only' describe wet earth giving way. yohomanic shares its root with yoh 'undo', three sentences on, and chiumaric comes back below as chiumar 'dissolved in water'; the others are glossed from the context and from Brasseur's French (without cohesion, without consistency, without strength, watery), and are guesses. xa ꜩubulic: the ligature is unclear here and Brasseur's OCR is lost; tz or tz' is undecided. xa vvlanic is printed as the manuscript writes it (xavvlanic; Brasseur xav'ulanic); a root vul 'collapse, tear down' is likely but not certain. vholom 'its head'; hum benac 'gone one way' (hun 'one' + be 'go' + -enac, like petenac); culuvach, with vach 'face, eye', is taken as 'veiled sight'; colol 'turning' is inferred. chirih 'behind it', from the relational noun 'back'.

sentences.t: Chi chau nabec, mahabi vnaoh; xa huzuc chiumar pa ha; mavi ꜭo.
sentences.l: It-spoke at-first, there-was-not its-mind; only suddenly it-dissolved in water; not it-was.
sentences.i: It did speak at first, but it had no mind; at once it dissolved in the water and was no more.
sentences.n: chau is ꜭhau 'speak', written with plain ch: Ximénez does not always mark ch'. nabec 'at first'. vnaoh 'its mind, its understanding', the naoh with which the creators planned the world. mavi ꜭo 'it was not': it could not stand, it did not last.

sentences.t: Xeꜭha chi cu ri Ahꜯac, Ahbit: “Cauach labec ta chuxoc, xa labe mavi chi binic, ma pu chi pocotahic. Ta chuxoc xa vnaoh chiri,” xecha.
sentences.l: They-said again then the He-who-builds, He-who-shapes: “Whatever(?) omen(?) let-it-be, only omen(?) not it-walks, nor also it-multiplies. Let-it-be only its-thought there,” they-said.
sentences.i: Then the Builder and the Shaper spoke again: “Let it be what it may, it is only a sign: it cannot walk, it cannot multiply. Let it remain a thought, then,” they said.
sentences.n: Ahꜯac, Ahbit 'he who builds, he who shapes' are titles made with ah- on the roots of Ꜯacol, Bitol. chi cu (and chi cut below) is probably chic 'again' with its c run into the next word, as in the shared letters above; the toggle shows chik, as there. This speech is obscure. labe may be a word for an omen or sign, and cauach labec ... xa labe is guessed as 'whatever it may be, it is only a sign'; the meaning is uncertain. binic 'walking' (bin, as in ibinibal); pocotahic 'multiplying', from the poc of the blessing on the deer and birds. Ta chuxoc xa vnaoh chiri 'let it be only a thought there' is read as giving the mud person up: let it go back to being a plan. Brasseur took it the other way, 'let a being with understanding be made there'.

sentences.t: Ta xqui yoh cut, xqui yoc chic ri qui ꜯac, qui bit.
sentences.l: Then they undid-it then, they broke-up again the their built, their shaped.
sentences.i: Then they undid it; they broke up again what they had built and shaped.
sentences.n: yoh 'undo, take apart' and yoc 'break up' (sense inferred) are a couplet of unmaking that answers ꜯac, bit, building and shaping.

sentences.t: Xeꜭha chi cut: “Hupacha qui chi ca bano chuꜩin ta vi, chi nauachir ta vi ꜫihiloy quech, ziquiy quech?” xecha, ta xqui naohih chic: “Xa ca byih chique Xpiyacoc, Xmucane, Hunahpu Vuch, Hunahpu Vtiu: Qui tiha chic vꜫihixic, vbitaxic.”
sentences.l: They-said again then: “How (?) let we make that-it-succeed then, that-it-take-shape then honourer of-us, caller of-us?” they-said, then they planned again: “Only let-us say to-them Xpiyacoc, Xmucane, Hunahpu Opossum, Hunahpu Coyote: Try again its-being-dayed, its-being-shaped.”
sentences.i: And they spoke again: “How shall we make it come right, so that there take shape those who will honour us, those who will call on us?” they said, and they took counsel again: “Let us speak to Xpiyacoc and Xmucane, Hunahpu Opossum and Hunahpu Coyote: Try once more: let its days be counted, let it be shaped.”
sentences.n: Hupacha qui chi ca bano: after a line-final qui- the next line starts with a struck-out qu; the qui itself was not struck and is printed, but Brasseur omits it and it may be a slip. Without it, chi ca bano 'shall we make'. chuꜩin 'that it come right', from vꜩ 'good'. ꜫihiloy quech, ziquiy quech 'honourers of us, callers of us': agent nouns in -oy, -iy, with quech 'ours'. The creators turn to the elders named in the preamble. vꜫihixic 'its being day-counted', from ꜫih 'day', is taken as divination by the days of the calendar, the work of a day-keeper; vbitaxic 'its being shaped'. byih is printed for MS byyh, as above. qui tiha 'try, you all!'. The speech within the speech is given without inner quotation marks.

sentences.t: Xe vꜭhan qui quib Ahꜯac, Ahbit. Ta xqui byih cut chire Xpiyacoc, Xmucane.
sentences.l: They spoke-together their selves He-who-builds, He-who-shapes. Then they said then to-him/her Xpiyacoc, Xmucane.
sentences.i: So the Builder and the Shaper spoke together. Then they spoke to Xpiyacoc and Xmucane.
sentences.n: xe vꜭhan qui quib 'they spoke among themselves': vꜭhan is the word for speech met in the first part (nabe vchan 'first speech'). chire 'to him, to her' (chi + r- 'him' + e) is singular: the old pair is spoken to as one, as in catoc below.

sentences.t: Cate cut vbixic ri chiquech ri e nicvachinel, Ratit Ꜫih, Ratit Zac, que vꜭhaxic cumal ri Ꜯacol, Bitol; are qui bi ri Xpiyacoc, Xmucane.
sentences.l: Then then its-saying the to-them the they diviners, Grandmother of-Day, Grandmother of-Light, as they-are-called by the Builder, Shaper; this-is their name the Xpiyacoc, Xmucane.
sentences.i: Then it was told to the diviners, Grandmother of the Day, Grandmother of the Light, as the Builder and the Shaper call them; their names are Xpiyacoc and Xmucane.
sentences.n: A paragraph sign stands before cate cut in the manuscript. chiquech 'to them'. e nicvachinel 'the diviners' (e makes it plural): an agent noun in -inel built with vach 'face, eye'; the first syllable is unclear, and 'diviner' is inferred from what the pair are asked to do. Ratit 'its grandmother', r- + atit: Ratit Ꜫih, Ratit Zac 'grandmother of the day, grandmother of the light', ꜫih being both 'day' and 'sun'. Ximénez's looped letter is read t, as Brasseur. are qui bi 'that is their name'.

sentences.t: Xeꜭha cu ri Huracan ruꜭ Tepeu, Ꜫucumaꜩ, ta xqui byih chirech ahꜫih, ahbit, e nicvachinel: “Xuculu; xa pu chu rico, cheta chic chi cavinac bitoh, chi cavinac ꜯacoh, ta chic ꜩucul, cool, coh ziquixtah, coh nabaxtah puch.
sentences.l: They-said then the Huracan with Sovereign, Quetzal-Serpent, then they said to-him/her day-keeper, shaper, they diviners: “Xuculu(?); only also let-it-find, let-it-be-known(?) now that our-person shaped, that our-person built, then now provider, sustainer, we called-upon, we remembered(?) also.
sentences.i: Then Huracan, with Tepeu and Q'ucumatz, spoke to the day-keeper, the shaper, the diviners: “Xuculu! Let it be found, let it be known now how our person may be shaped, our person built, to provide and to sustain, so that we may be called upon and remembered.
sentences.n: Ximénez writes qu ri here; Brasseur's cu is printed. ahꜫih 'he of the day', the day-keeper who counts the calendar (ah- + ꜫih), still the K'iche' word for a calendar priest; ahbit 'shaper'. chirech 'to him, to her' is singular, as chire above: the pair is addressed as one. Xuculu is printed as the manuscript writes it, as one word; Brasseur divides X-a culu. Its meaning is unknown, and it is left untranslated. chu rico 'let it find' (rico 'find', as in xe rico quib in the first part); cheta is uncertain and is read 'let it be known'. cavinac 'our person' (ca- + vinac); bitoh, ꜯacoh 'shaped, built': the creators' two roots again. ziquixtah, nabaxtah: the passives of ziquih and nabax with tah, the particle of wishing, joined on: 'so that we may be called on, remembered'.

sentences.t: Catoc ta cut pa ꜩih, Iyom, Mamom, catit, camam, Xpiyacoc, Xmucane; cha tah ta chauaxoc, ta zaquiroc, caziquixic, catoquexic, canabaxic rumal vinac ꜯac, vinac bit, vinac poy, vinac anom. Cha ta chuxoc.”
sentences.l: Enter then then into word, Midwife, Grandfather, our-grandmother, our-grandfather, Xpiyacoc, Xmucane; say let then will-be-sown, then will-dawn, our-being-called-upon, our-being-prayed-to(?), our-being-remembered(?) by person built, person shaped, person effigy, person anom(?). Say then let-it-be.”
sentences.i: Come into the counsel, then, Midwife and Grandfather, our grandmother, our grandfather, Xpiyacoc, Xmucane: let there be sowing, let there be dawn, so that we are called upon, prayed to and remembered by the person built, the person shaped, the person of effigy, the person of figure. Let it be so.”
sentences.n: catoc 'you enter': c- + at 'you (one)' + oc 'enter'; the grandmother and grandfather are addressed as one and invited pa ꜩih 'into the word', into the council. catit, camam 'our grandmother, our grandfather' (ca- 'our' + atit, mam; the looped letter read t, as in Ratit), beside their titles Iyom, Mamom from the preamble. cha tah ta chauaxoc, ta zaquiroc repeats the creators' wish from the first part almost word for word. Three passive nouns with ca- 'our': 'our being called on', catoquexic (sense uncertain, 'prayed to' is a guess), 'our being remembered'. vinac poy: poy is an effigy or doll (Brasseur 'manikin'); anom is unexplained, and 'figure' is a guess. The speech goes on in the next part.

about: The creators now think of the animals: the creatures of the mountains, deer and birds, puma and jaguar, snakes, to be guardians of the forests. They give each its home, the deer in the canyons and the grass, the birds in the tops of the trees, and then tell them to speak and to call on their makers by name. But the animals can only screech and chatter and howl, each in its own way, and cannot say the creators' names. So the creators change their word: the animals will have the canyons and forests for their home, and their service will be their flesh, to be killed and eaten. The creators try again to make a person who will honour and sustain them, and build one of earth and mud. It is a failure: it crumbles and goes soft, cannot turn its head or look behind it, speaks without understanding, and soon dissolves in the water; they take it apart. Then they decide to consult the old pair Xpiyacoc and Xmucane, the diviners, Grandmother of the Day and Grandmother of the Light, and Huracan, with Tepeu and Q'ucumatz, invites them into the council to find how a person may be shaped and built.
